title: review: S2a2 packet memory wiring: HOT view plus filtered WARM search feed the gotchas and decisions packet sections in shadow, decision_log kind memory_retrieval, promotion feature memory_tiers (P1, P3, P5 groundwork)
spec:
In orchestrator/spawn.py _packet_body: today the gotchas section comes from memory_recall over notes+bus (up to 5 hits) and the decisions section from grep of decisions.md in the worktree. Add a second source: hot = memory_hot.build (read HOT.md when fresh, i.e. store unchanged since the last build, else rebuild) and warm = memory_store.search(query from task title + scope basenames, kind in (gotcha, decision, architecture), file filter per scope path, limit 8) merged and deduplicated by id, rendered with the same one-line format, capped by [memory].packet_hot_tokens (default 1200, dated comment). Mode [memory].mode (off|shadow|active; add as shadow with a dated comment) and promotion FEATURES entry memory_tiers (orchestrator/promotion.py) with criteria: at least 30 decision_log rows of kind memory_retrieval in 7 days and a measured presented-token reduction with no rise in fix rounds (state the criteria in the feature entry as the other features do). Shadow: present the legacy sections unchanged, compute the tiered sections and record one decision_log row kind memory_retrieval (add it to decision_log.KINDS) with candidates (record ids with tier and score), selected (ids the tiered path would present), legacy_ids (the hits the legacy path presented), tokens_legacy, tokens_tiered, mode, subject task id. Active: present the tiered sections and still record the row. Off: legacy only. packet_meta gains memory_mode and memory_ids. The row must never raise into packet building (guard, log a warning). Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/07-hot-memory.md gains a section on packet wiring and the shadow comparison measured on three real tasks of this repository (ids, tokens_legacy vs tokens_tiered).
Spec review T-1133 folded in: (1) Promotion: FEATURES entries carry no per-feature criteria; register memory_tiers as {table: memory, key: mode, modes, default shadow, evidence: retrieval} and add a promotion.collect() branch that counts decision_log rows of that kind (n plus tokens_legacy/tokens_tiered sums) so the global CRITERIA (min_samples etc.) apply as for every other feature; drop the '30 rows in 7 days' wording. (2) Decision kind: reuse the existing, unused CONTEXT_KINDS entry 'retrieval' for these rows (no new memory_retrieval kind); document in decision_log.py that retrieval rows are memory retrievals. (3) Packet size: the hot and warm lines are rendered into the existing gotchas and decisions sections, capped first by [memory].packet_hot_tokens (chars/4), and those sections stay in the existing trimmable tuple so the 4800-char body trim loop still applies after; no second cap. (4) Freshness: spawn compares the mtime of .orchestrator/memory/index.sqlite with the mtime of HOT.md (same mtime-signature idea as bus.py near line 258); HOT.md newer or equal means fresh, else memory_hot.build() is called once. (5) memory_store.search takes one kind: call it once per kind (gotcha, decision, architecture) and merge by id. (6) pool.toml comment for [memory].mode includes the revert instruction ('revert by setting mode back to off').
Spec review T-1150 folded in: (1) Packet building NEVER calls memory_hot.build(): _packet_body reads HOT.md as it is and records hot_fresh (bool, from the mtime comparison) on the retrieval row and packet_meta; the daemon's single-threaded tick (daemon.py joins the scope) calls memory_hot.build() at most once per tick, before dispatch, when HOT.md is stale or missing, under a module-level threading.Lock in memory_hot; memory_store._open (scope adds orchestrator/memory_store.py) sets journal_mode WAL and busy_timeout 5000 so concurrent readers never see 'database is locked'. (2) promotion.collect for memory_tiers fills fix_rounds_delta: mean fix rounds per task over tasks whose retrieval row has mode active minus the same mean over tasks whose row has mode shadow, computed from constraints.fix_round_for counts on the bus; None only while either side has fewer than 5 tasks, and the docs say so. (3) Warm query: exactly three memory_store.search calls per packet build (kind gotcha, decision, architecture) with the free-text query built from the task title words plus scope path basenames without extension; no file= filter (search's file filter is exact-match and is not used here).
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_spawn.py::test_packet_memory_shadow_keeps_legacy_sections_and_logs_row (shadow: legacy text presented, memory_retrieval row with both token counts)
tests/test_spawn.py::test_packet_memory_active_presents_tiered_sections (active: HOT and warm hits presented, capped by packet_hot_tokens)
tests/test_daemon.py::test_tick_rebuilds_hot_at_most_once_when_stale (two stale ticks in a row rebuild once each; packet building never rebuilds)

comments.issue: decision_log.record() for kind="retrieval" passes candidates=retrieval["candidates"] (a list of dicts like {"id":..,"tier":..,"score":..}) but selected=selected (a list of plain id strings), and does not pass rejected= explicitly. decision_log.record()'s auto-compute is `rejected = [c for c in candidates if c not in selected_values]`; since a dict never equals a string, every candidate fails the `not in` check and rejected always equals the full candidate list, even for candidates that were actually selected. Every retrieval decision_log row therefore records rejected == candidates regardless of what memory was actually chosen, corrupting the evidence trail this feature is meant to produce. Other call sites (e.g. skill_selection at spawn.py:110) avoid this by passing rejected explicitly; this call site should do the same (e.g. rejected=[c for c in candidates if c["id"] not in selected], or pass selected as the matching candidate dicts).

events.reason: Planner: root T-1151 merged by hand after the rebase; review T-1171 approved the same content
